Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/policies/terms.en.html

# Terms of Use

Last updated: 2026-11-13.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./terms.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## Who these terms cover

These terms cover everyone who reads Nusquama's site and repository, everyone who applies for knighting, and everyone whose name is on the roll of knights.
A person who applies for knighting agrees, in the application form, to the version of these terms in force on that day.
Reading the site or the repository is not taken as agreement to anything; for readers, these terms describe how Nusquama works, and the law decides what each side owes.
The agreement on courts is made only with those who agreed in the application form for knighting ("Governing law and disputes").
The [Disclaimer](./disclaimer.en.md), [Privacy](./privacy.en.md), the [Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), the [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md) and [Names and rights](./names.en.md) are also part of these terms.
The reasons the operator believes Nusquama breaks no law are set out, law by law, in the [Legality Statement](./legality.en.md). The Legality Statement is not part of these terms; it explains the operator's understanding.

## What Nusquama is

Nusquama is a work of fiction that the operator writes for fun.
It is not a state. It has no territory, people, government, currency, passports or nationality, and it claims no sovereignty and no land.
It is not a state under international law, seeks no recognition as a state, and enters into no diplomatic relations with any state.
It is not related to any real state, royal house, order of knighthood, honours system, decoration or title, and it neither claims to be one nor replaces one.
It issues no currency, points, vouchers, electronic value, passports, identity documents or certificates.
"Knight-King Nemo I" is the name of a role the operator plays in the fiction.

## No ill intent, and obeying the law

Nusquama means no harm. It does not aim to deceive anyone or to hurt anyone.
The operator runs Nusquama in compliance with the laws of Japan and with the terms of the services it uses.
If the operator learns that something may break a law, the operator stops that part first, then checks it and fixes it.
When it is unclear whether something is lawful, the operator chooses not to do it.

## Titles

Nusquama's titles (Knight-King, knight, member of the Order of Errata) are words inside a work of fiction.
None of them is a title set by the law of any country, and none carries legal effect, status or privileges.
Knighting does not confer a decoration, honour or rank of knighthood (including a rank in an order) of any country; it records on the roll the account name of a person who joined the game. The name of knight is a role name inside the fiction that goes with that entry.
The titles are used only inside the kingdom.
Inside the kingdom means this repository, the site, and the articles and posts the operator wrote to introduce Nusquama (listed in the [README](../README.md), in Japanese, under "ほかの場所").
Nusquama makes and hands out no physical decorations, insignia, uniforms or certificates.
The titles must not be used in a way that could be mistaken for an official post, court rank, decoration, academic degree or any other title set by law.
Nusquama's titles must not be written on a CV, a paper, a business card, an official document, in commerce or in advertising.
From 2026-11-22, the name of knight is used only in connection with Nusquama.
From 2026-11-22, the name of knight is never presented as a title of nobility, an honour, an order, a rank or a dignity of any state, and is not used in an official, commercial or legal context.
From 2026-11-22, if this is breached, the operator removes the name from the roll ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Use of the name of knight").

## Fees

Nusquama charges no one anything.
It sells no titles, takes no donations, shows no advertising and sells nothing.
Applying for knighting and being listed on the roll are free.
Anyone who claims to grant Nusquama's titles for a fee has nothing to do with Nusquama.

## What is not allowed

- Applying for knighting with someone else's error or with a correction that is not your own.
- Writing another person's personal information (real name, address, contact details, photographs and so on) in an issue.
- Defaming, threatening or harassing anyone.
- Using Nusquama's titles or emblem as if they were a real title, decoration or the insignia of a real organisation.
- Collecting money or goods in Nusquama's name.
- Trying to break the site or the forms.
- Ticking a box in the application form for something that is not true, such as your age, the country you live in, your nationality, or that the correction is of your own error.

The operator may refuse such applications, close the issues, and remove names from the roll.
If a ticked box turns out to be untrue, the operator removes the name from the roll as soon as the operator learns of it. From 2026-11-22, the operator may also refuse further applications from the same GitHub account.
The operator relies on the ticked boxes in good faith and does not check them. A person knighted on an untrue box does not mean that Nusquama accepts applications from a country, or from holders of a nationality, from which it says it does not.
The ticked boxes stay in the public issue until it is deleted at the person's request, so that what was ticked, and when, can be shown.
Nothing here asks an applicant for a penalty, or for damages beyond what the law provides.

## No warranty

The site and the repository are provided as they are.
The operator does not promise that they can always be read or that their content is free of errors.
The [Disclaimer](./disclaimer.en.md) has the details.

## Changes and ending

These terms and the other pages may change.
The date on each page shows its last change, and earlier versions remain in the public repository.
The dates on the pages, and in the timeline, the gazette, the errata and the roll, are dates in Japan time.
The day a text was fetched is the day in UTC that the record of the fetch keeps.
The founding day, 2026-11-07, is also a date in UTC.
A change that is unfavourable to readers or knights will be shown on this page, with its content and the date it takes effect, before it takes effect.
Notice: from 2026-11-22, only people who live in Japan and are in Japan when they apply may apply for knighthood; nationality does not matter, except that people who hold Italian nationality, or the nationality of a country that restricts foreign titles, are excluded ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Who may apply").
Notice: from 2026-11-22, people who hold Italian nationality may not apply for knighthood, even if they live in Japan, and even if they also hold another nationality ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Who may apply").
Notice: from 2026-11-22, people who hold the nationality of a country that restricts accepting foreign titles may not apply for knighthood, even if they live in Japan, and even if they also hold another nationality ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Countries that restrict foreign titles").
Notice: from 2026-11-22, the name of knight is used only in connection with Nusquama, is never presented as a title of nobility, an honour, an order, a rank or a dignity of any state, and is not used in an official, commercial or legal context; if this is breached, the name is removed from the roll ("Titles").
Notice: from 2026-11-22, knighting presumes that the applicant is a person of good sense who treats the title as play, and an application without the box for this premise ticked is not accepted ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "The premise of good sense").
Notice: from 2026-11-22, further applications from a GitHub account that ticked a box untruly may be refused ("What is not allowed").
From 2026-11-12 until 00:00 on 2026-11-22 (Japan time), applications for knighting are not received ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "Pause in receiving applications"). This rests on the provision in "No ill intent, and obeying the law" for stopping a part when a risk of breaking the law is found.
No change will ever create a fee.
Nusquama may end without notice. If it ends, the roll of knights stays in the repository unless a knight asks to withdraw.

## Governing law and disputes

These terms are governed by Japanese law.
Nothing in these terms limits a right that the law does not allow to be limited.
Disputes are to be settled by agreement first.
Before bringing any claim, the operator first talks with the other party.
The talks take place in an issue. When the other party has made a contact public on their own GitHub profile, they may also take place at that contact ([Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md), "Requests that cannot be made in public").
If the other party offers to settle, the operator responds in good faith.
A dispute not settled by agreement goes, according to the amount in dispute, to the Utsunomiya District Court or the Utsunomiya Summary Court, as the court of first instance by agreement, for a person who has agreed to these terms in the application form for knighting, and only for suits based on these terms or on that person's own application for knighting, listing on the roll of knights or withdrawal.
This agreement is not exclusive.
Any other dispute, and any dispute with a person who has not agreed in the form, goes to the court that the law sets.
When the operator brings a suit against a person these terms cover, the operator brings it only in the Utsunomiya District Court or the Utsunomiya Summary Court, or in the court with jurisdiction over the place of that person's general forum.
When the other party brings a suit in the Utsunomiya District Court or the Utsunomiya Summary Court, the operator does not contest jurisdiction, whatever the dispute.
This does not take away the right of a consumer, or of a person outside Japan, to sue in another court where the law allows it.

## GitHub's and Vercel's terms

Nusquama runs on two services in the United States. Applications and requests are received in GitHub issues, and the site is served by Vercel.
Their own terms apply alongside these terms. These terms do not bind GitHub or Vercel, and a dispute with either follows its own terms.
Their terms were read at their sources on 2026-11-09: GitHub's [Terms of Service](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service) (effective 2026-04-27), [Acceptable Use Policies](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/acceptable-use-policies/github-acceptable-use-policies) and [General Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement) (effective 2026-04-27); Vercel's [Terms of Service](https://vercel.com/legal/terms) (last updated 2026-10-19), [Acceptable Use Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/acceptable-use-policy) (last updated 2026-04-21) and [Privacy Notice](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-notice) (last updated 2026-06-01).
What they say that matters to people who use Nusquama:

- GitHub accepts only users aged 13 or over (GitHub Terms, B.3). Knighthood can be applied for only from the age of 16.
- What is written in an issue must follow GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies, among them its rules on spam, harassment and other people's private information (GitHub Terms, C).
- GitHub may refuse or remove content that breaks the law or its terms, and may close accounts (GitHub Terms, D.2 and M.3).
- Content in a public repository and in its issues can be seen by everyone, and GitHub's terms do not restrict its lawful use by others (GitHub Terms, D.5 and D.8). GitHub and its affiliates may store, copy and display it, and use it to train AI features and the models of their affiliates (GitHub Terms, D.4); there is no setting that turns this off for public content (GitHub Terms, J.3).
- The site is served on Vercel's free Hobby plan, which Vercel allows only for personal or non-commercial use; Nusquama is non-commercial. Vercel may disable or remove a deployment on that plan with or without notice, so the site can go offline without warning; the roll and the rules stay in the repository (Vercel Terms, section 4).
- On the Hobby plan, Vercel may use the content it serves to train AI and machine learning models, and share it with third parties for that purpose, unless the account turns this off in its team settings (Vercel Terms, section 3).
- Content on the site must also follow Vercel's Acceptable Use Policy, and Vercel may remove or disable content (Vercel Terms, sections 3 and 8).
- GitHub and Vercel each provide their services "as is", without warranty, and limit their liability (GitHub Terms, O and P; Vercel Terms, sections 20 and 21). Their terms are governed by the law of California, with the courts of San Francisco, and Vercel's also provide for arbitration (GitHub Terms, S.1; Vercel Terms, section 23).

## Contact

Contact is by [issue](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/nusquama/issues) in the repository.
There is no private channel. The operator answers privately only in the case described under "Requests that cannot be made in public" in the [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md).

# Disclaimer

Last updated: 2026-11-12.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./disclaimer.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

This page gathers in one place what Nusquama does not promise and what Nusquama is not.
This page is part of the [Terms of Use](./terms.en.md). Where this page and the main text of the Terms differ, the main text of the Terms applies.

## A work of fiction

Nusquama is a work of fiction written for fun.
It is not a state, government, local authority, royal house, noble family, order of knighthood, religious body, or system of decorations or honours.
It is not a state under international law, seeks no recognition as a state, and claims no country's territory.
The Founding Declaration, the Basic Law, the Ten Precepts and the emblem are documents inside the fiction.
Nusquama means no harm. It does not aim to deceive anyone or to hurt anyone.
The promise of no ill intent and of obeying the law is made in the Terms of Use, under "No ill intent, and obeying the law".

## Titles have no effect

Names such as Knight-King, knight and member of the Order of Errata are words inside the fiction.
No country's law sets them, and they carry no legal effect, status, privileges or honour.
Knighting is not the award of a real honour.
Having a name on the roll does not show that the person holds any qualification or position.

## Relation to real things

Nusquama has no relation to any of the following.

- Real states, royal houses, governments and local authorities
- Real orders of knighthood, religious military orders, decorations, and systems of honours (including the Japanese honours system and the British honours system)
- Every so-called micronation (self-declared nation) other than Nusquama
- Novels, films, games, animation and other works based on the Arthurian legends, and their rights holders
- Anyone who publishes or adapts Thomas More's Utopia or Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
- Any music group, work, organisation, person or product that uses the same name as Nusquama or Nemo, or a similar one

## Statements outside the kingdom

Inside the kingdom means only this repository, the site, and the articles and posts listed in the README under "ほかの場所", as the Terms of Use set out under the handling of titles.
A post or statement not listed there is outside the kingdom, even if the operator wrote it.
The rules of Nusquama do not reach it, and what is said there is not a promise of Nusquama.
Nusquama has no relation to the operator's other activities either.
The titles of Nusquama are not used in those activities, and Nusquama does not recommend them.
Nusquama has no plan to obtain a domain of its own. Its only site is https://nusquama.vercel.app/.
A site under another domain that calls itself Nusquama is outside the kingdom and has no relation to the operator.

Where the words "Nusquama", "Nemo" and "Mukau" come from is written in [Names and rights](./names.en.md). None of them shows a tie to any particular work or organisation.

## The operator's research

Nusquama is separate from the operator's research and is not part of it.
Nusquama is never presented as a research output.
The pages of Nusquama do not link to the operator's research pages, and the research pages do not link to Nusquama.

## Applications for knighting

Applications for knighting are received as public issues.
The operator does not vouch that the correction described in an application is right.
A name on the roll does not mean the operator recommends that person's correction, research or character.

## Accuracy and availability

The site and the repository are provided as they are.
The operator does not promise that they are free of errors, can always be read, or will continue.
The site is served by Vercel, and the repository and issues are kept by GitHub. If those services stop, Nusquama can no longer be read.
GitHub and Vercel each provide their services "as is", without warranty, and limit their liability under their own terms; Nusquama cannot promise more about their services than they do.
The site is served on Vercel's free Hobby plan, on which Vercel may disable or remove a deployment with or without notice. What their terms provide is set out in the [Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), under "GitHub's and Vercel's terms".

## Not advice

Nusquama's documents are not legal or professional advice.
Where the pages touch on law, they set out the operator's understanding, not a legal judgement.
The law-by-law analysis is in the [Legality Statement](./legality.en.md). It has not been reviewed by a lawyer.

## Liability

Nusquama is a free work of fiction.
Except in cases of intent or gross negligence, the operator accepts no liability for damage arising from use of the site or the repository.
Where the Japanese Consumer Contract Act applies, the previous sentence does not apply. In that case the operator is liable as that Act and the Civil Code provide, including for damage caused by slight negligence.
Nothing here excludes or limits any liability the law does not allow to be excluded or limited.
The responsibility for anything a knight, a reader or a third party does against the rules, or outside them, lies with that person.
Except where the law makes the operator responsible, the operator is not responsible for such acts.
Those of such acts that come near a law's elements, and the operator's caution, are listed in the [Legality Statement](./legality.en.md), "Acts outside the rules that come near a law's elements".

## How this was made

Nusquama's text, emblem and site were written with Claude Code (Anthropic) at the operator's request.
The operator checked them and is responsible for them. Claude is neither a knight nor a king, and is not an author of Nusquama.
Nusquama is not affiliated with Anthropic and is not endorsed by it.

# Privacy

Last updated: 2026-11-13.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./privacy.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## Who handles the data

The operator of Nusquama, an individual who owns the GitHub account cpsbvbng26-dotcom.
The operator handles personal data in line with Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information.
The operator's name and address are given without delay to the person who asks for them, at a contact that person has made public on their own GitHub profile.
To ask, choose 「非公開の連絡を求める」 ("Ask for a private contact") as the kind in the [Requests](./requests.en.md) form.
For a person with no such contact, there is no private route to give the name and address. They are not written in the issue ([Requests](./requests.en.md), "Requests that cannot be made in public").

## What the site collects

The site uses no cookies and has no analytics and no advertising.
The pages of the site request nothing from any other server.
The site is served by Vercel (United States). To serve it, Vercel may process and log requests, including IP addresses. Vercel handles them under its own privacy policy.

## What an application for knighthood involves

Applications for knighthood are received as public issues on GitHub (United States).
An application involves:

- The GitHub account name
- A public link to the correction
- An account of what was wrong and how it was corrected

These are public in the issue. For those knighted, the GitHub account name, the day of knighting, a summary of the mistake corrected and a link to the application are put on the [roll of knights](../KNIGHTS.en.md).
No real name, address, affiliation or contact details are asked for, and the form asks applicants not to write them.
Nothing sensitive, such as illness, disability, belief or criminal record, is asked for either, and the form asks applicants not to write it.
But if the linked correction gives a real name or affiliation, the roll and the issue publicly connect the account name with that person.
Issues are also subject to GitHub's Terms of Service and Privacy Statement.
When an application issue is opened or edited, an automatic check in GitHub Actions reads the ticks in the form and the text of the link to the correction.
The automatic check does not open the link to the correction. It sends no request to the linked site, and keeps nothing of what is there.
The operator is the one who opens and reads the linked page ([Rules on Knighting](./knighting.en.md), "What the operator checks").

## What a report of a mistake involves

Reports of mistakes in the King's texts are received as public issues on GitHub (United States), through the form [誤りの知らせ (Report a mistake)](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/nusquama/issues/new?template=error.yml).
A report involves the GitHub account name and what the report says.
These are public in the issue. The King's errata do not name the person who reported the mistake.
No real name, address, affiliation or contact details are asked for, and the form asks reporters not to write them.

## Purposes of use

To decide on knighting, to keep the roll, to answer requests, and to check reported mistakes and record them in the King's errata. Nothing else.

## Providing data to others, and businesses in other countries

The information above is public on the services of GitHub and Vercel, both in the United States.
An applicant agrees, by a pledge in the form, to its being public and handled by these services.
The United States has no federal law that covers personal data comprehensively, like Japan's Act on the Protection of Personal Information. There are state laws, and the rights a person has differ by state and sector. There is no single authority for personal data for the whole country.
According to the survey of the Personal Information Protection Commission (as of October 2021), the United States has no adequacy decision of the EU and has taken part in the APEC CBPR system since 25 July 2012. The same survey lists, for the United States, no system that obliges businesses to cooperate with government collection of information in a way that may seriously affect the rights and interests of the person ([Personal Information Protection Commission, "外国制度（アメリカ合衆国）"](https://www.ppc.go.jp/enforcement/infoprovision/laws/offshore_report_america/), in Japanese).
GitHub's measures are in [GitHub's Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement), and Vercel's in [Vercel's Privacy Notice](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-notice).
The operator cannot confirm whether GitHub and Vercel take all the measures that correspond to the eight principles of the OECD Privacy Guidelines, because how they handle data inside can only be known from the policies they publish (Article 17(4) of the Enforcement Rules of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information). The difference that is known is their own use of public content, set out in the next paragraph.
There are two cases in which GitHub and Vercel use public content themselves, each set out in their terms; Nusquama cannot change them. GitHub's Terms of Service allow GitHub and its affiliates to use what is placed in issues and public repositories (including the applications and the roll) for AI features and to train the models of its affiliates (D.4). There is no setting to stop this for public content (J.3). Vercel's Terms of Service allow Vercel, on the free Hobby plan that serves Nusquama, to use the content of the site (including the roll) to train AI and machine-learning models, and to give it to third parties for that purpose, unless the account's team turns this off (section 3).
If these uses worry you because of your personal data, do not apply. A knight may ask at any time to be taken off the roll, and their name is then taken off it.
GitHub and Vercel are not processors handling personal data on the operator's behalf. They are used as the place of publication and of serving, after their terms and policies were checked.
The operator considers listing on the roll to be a provision to an unspecified large number of people. Its record (Article 29 of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information) is the repository history in which the row was added. The history keeps the day the row was added, the account name and the items listed. A row is added only for a person who ticked every pledge in the application form.
The operator receives no personal data from third parties. What it handles is only what the person writes and the link to the correction the person made public.
Except where the law requires, nothing is given to any other third party.

## How long data is kept

An entry on the roll is kept until a request to withdraw.
The issue of a declined application is kept, to show the one sentence of the decline; it is deleted if the applicant asks.
On a request to delete, the operator deletes the issue, or empties its body and removes the earlier versions from its edit history too.
The history of the repository, and copies already made by others, may still hold an entry.

## Security measures

The only personal data handled is what is in the public issues and on the roll of knights. It is gathered nowhere else and no other copy is made.
Only the operator's GitHub account, which owns the repository, can change the roll and the site.
That account uses two-factor authentication.
Every change to the roll and the site is kept in the public history of the repository and goes in only after passing the checks.
The site has no cookies and no database, and collects nothing from its readers.
How handling in other countries is prepared for is set out above, under "Providing data to others, and businesses in other countries".

## If a leak or the like occurs

If a leak, loss or damage of personal data occurs that the law requires to be reported, the operator reports it to the Personal Information Protection Commission.
The persons concerned are then told too, in their application issue or on the page of the roll.
If the operator's GitHub account is taken over and the roll is altered or erased, this is treated in the same way.

## Requests for disclosure, correction, suspension of use and deletion

Anyone may ask at any time for an entry about them to be corrected or deleted, or to be taken off the roll.
Requests for disclosure of retained personal data and for suspension of its use are also met.
The procedure is in [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](./requests.en.md). There is no charge.
Any matter that Article 32 of the Act on the Protection of Personal Information requires to be made known and that is not on this page is answered without delay on request.
Complaints about the handling of personal data are received through the same request form.

## Minors

A person under 16 may not apply for knighthood.
The Q&A of the Personal Information Protection Commission says that, in general, the consent of a legal representative or the like is needed for children up to the age of 12 to 15 ([Q&A](https://www.ppc.go.jp/personalinfo/faq/APPI_QA/), Q1-62, checked on 2026-11-08). Nusquama has no means to check such consent, so it accepts no application from a person under 16.
When an application turns out to be from a person under 16, the name is taken off the roll and the issue is deleted, without being asked.

## Changes to this policy

When this policy changes, the date on this page is changed.
Earlier versions remain in the public repository.

# Rules on Knighting

Last updated: 2026-11-13.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./knighting.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## What knighting is

Knighting is giving the name of knight, within a work of fiction.
It brings no legal effect, status, privilege or honour.
Knighting does not confer a decoration, honour or rank of knighthood of any country.
Knighting is free. It is never given in exchange for money, goods or services (Basic Law, Article 6).
Knighting issues no document or object, such as a letter of appointment, a certificate or an insignia. It only puts an account name on the roll.

## Who may apply

A person who has publicly corrected one of their own mistakes.
The correction must be public and checkable by anyone, such as an erratum to a paper, a note added to a blog post or article, a fix to code, or a statement withdrawn.
A person under 16 may not apply.
A person whom the law of the country where they live forbids to receive or use a title of knighthood given by a private person may not apply either. For example, Article 8 of Italy's Law No. 178 of 1951 forbids private persons and bodies to confer titles of knighthood under any name.
From 2026-11-22, only people who live in Japan and are in Japan when they apply may apply. Nationality does not matter, except that people who hold Italian nationality, or the nationality of a country under "Countries that restrict foreign titles", are excluded.
From 2026-11-22, people who live outside Japan may not apply, whatever their nationality, because the laws outside Japan cannot all be checked country by country.
From 2026-11-22, a person who lives in Japan may not apply while outside Japan, for travel, business or study, because some foreign laws reach not only those who live there but those who are there.
From 2026-11-22, a person who holds Italian nationality may not apply, even if they live in Japan, and even if they also hold another nationality. There are two reasons.
First, by plain common sense, an Italian national becoming a knight of a Japanese micronation is out of place to begin with.
Second, Article 8 of Italy's Law No. 178 of 1951 also punishes anyone who uses such a title, and applies even when it was conferred abroad. An Italian national who received and used the title is the most realistic path by which that article could reach Nusquama.
This limit reduces the possibility that the article applies; it does not remove it ([Legality Statement](./legality.en.md), "Laws outside Japan").
A person who only stays in Japan briefly, such as a traveller, does not count as living in Japan.

## Pause in receiving applications

From 2026-11-12 until 00:00 on 2026-11-22 (Japan time), applications for knighting are not received. The owner decided this on 2026-11-12. The reason is that, in the period before the revised rules take effect on 2026-11-22 (only people who live and are in Japan; people who hold Italian nationality excluded; the premise of good sense), the possibility that laws outside Japan apply remained.
The pause rests on the Terms of Use, "No ill intent, and obeying the law" (when a risk of breaking the law is found, that part is stopped first, then checked and corrected).
An application issue opened during the pause gets a comment from the automatic check saying that applications are paused, and is closed as not accepted. The link to the correction is not opened.
From 00:00 on 2026-11-22 (Japan time), receiving resumes without anyone acting, and the revised rules are checked. An issue opened during the pause is not reopened; the applicant opens a new issue.
Claude decided on 2026-11-12 that whether an application is received depends on the time the issue was opened, how it is closed, and that a new issue is used, so that the pause depends on dates only and waits for no one.
On 2026-11-12, when the pause was decided, there were no open applications for knighting, and there was no knight on the roll.

## The premise of good sense

From 2026-11-22, knighting presumes that the applicant is a person of good sense who treats the title as play.
This premise means using the title only within the fiction, and keeping the following rules.

- Use the title only within the kingdom ([Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), "Titles"; Basic Law, Article 8).
- Do not present the title as if it were a real title, decoration or insignia of an organisation.
- Do not put the title on a CV, a paper, a business card, an official document, a business transaction or an advertisement.
- Do not sell the title, and do not use it to collect money or goods.
- Do not use the title to deceive anyone.

These set out, as ways of using the title, the rules in the Terms of Use ("Titles", "What is not allowed", "No ill intent, and obeying the law") and Article 8 of the Basic Law.
From 2026-11-22, the applicant ticks a box in the form for this premise.
If what the applicant wrote, or the linked correction, shows clearly that this premise does not hold, the applicant is not knighted ("What is declined").
If it becomes clear after knighting, the knighting is revoked under "Withdrawal and revocation".
When revoking, the operator writes in the application issue only which rule was not kept, briefly, and comments on no one. The issue is deleted if the person asks.


## Countries that restrict foreign titles

From 2026-11-22, a person who holds the nationality of any of the 15 countries in the table below may not apply, even if they live in Japan, and even if they also hold another nationality. Claude decided this on 2026-11-12.
On the texts fetched and read, the constitution or a law of each country in the table is of one of three types.

1. Type 1: it forbids accepting a foreign title, order, honour or rank, or requires the State's permission to accept one.
2. Type 2: it attaches loss of nationality or citizenship, or a penalty, to accepting a foreign title or the like.
3. Type 3: it punishes assuming a title of nobility that is not one's own, and the name of knight could be read as such a title.

Nusquama is not a state, and the name of knight is not a title of any country.
Even so, on the words of these provisions, a reading remains on which they apply.
The strictest reading was taken, and such applications are not accepted. This costs nothing, and not accepting them closes that path.
Some provisions bind only public officials or holders of State office. The operator does not check an applicant's office, so the whole nationality is excluded.

| Country | Provision relied on | Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bangladesh | Bangladesh 1972 (reinst. 1986, rev. 2018) 30. Prohibition of foreign titles, etc. | Type 1 |
| Belgium | Code pénal Art. 230 | Type 3 |
| Colombia | Colombia 1991 (rev. 2015) Article 129 | Type 1 |
| Dominican Republic | Dominican Republic 2015 Article 128. Powers of the President of the Republic (paragraph 23) | Type 1 |
| Honduras | Honduras 1982 (rev. 2013) Article 205 (paragraph 18) | Type 1 |
| Hungary | Hungary 2011 (rev. 2016) Article 9 (paragraph 21) | Type 1 |
| India | India 1949 (rev. 2023) 18. Abolition of titles | Type 1 |
| Ireland | Ireland 1937 (rev. 2019) ARTICLE 40, 2 | Type 1 |
| Mexico | Mexico 1917 (rev. 2015) Article 37 | Type 2 |
| Nepal | Nepal 2015 (rev. 2016) 277. Titles, honors, and decorations | Type 1 |
| Netherlands | Wetboek van Strafrecht Artikel 435 | Type 1, Type 2, Type 3 |
| Pakistan | Pakistan 1973 (reinst. 2002, rev. 2018) 259. Awards | Type 1 |
| Philippines | Philippines 1987 Sec 8 | Type 1 |
| United States of America | United States of America 1789 (rev. 1992) Article I, Section 9 | Type 1 |
| Venezuela | Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) 1999 (rev. 2009) Article 149; Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) 1999 (rev. 2009) Article 187 (paragraph 14) | Type 1 |

Besides the countries in the table, a person whose country of nationality has a law of any of the three types may not apply either, because the laws of countries not fetched may have the same provisions.
People who hold Italian nationality are excluded separately, under "Who may apply".
The texts of the provisions and the reasons for reading them so are in the [survey of the world's laws](../docs/world-law-2026-11-12.md) (in Japanese), "2026-11-12 の続き：当てはめ".
This limit reduces the possibility that these provisions apply; it does not remove it.

## Use of the name of knight

From 2026-11-22, the name of knight is used only within the following three rules. Claude decided this on 2026-11-12.

- Use it only in connection with Nusquama.
- Never present it as a title of nobility, an honour, an order, a rank or a dignity of any state.
- Do not use it in an official, commercial or legal context (documents, filings, contracts, courts and the like).

If it becomes known that these rules were breached, the name is removed from the roll.
The reason is that the following provisions, fetched and read, punish assuming titles, honours or ranks without the right to them, or using them without permission.

- Germany: Strafgesetzbuch (StGB) § 132a
- Argentina: Código Penal de la Nación (Ley 11.179, t.o. 1984) ARTICULO 247
- Mexico: Código Penal Federal Artículo 250
- Italy: Codice penale (R.D. 19 ottobre 1930, n. 1398) Art. 498 (paragraph 5); Legge 3 marzo 1951, n. 178 (Ordine al merito della Repubblica) Art. 7 (paragraph 2)
- Belgium: Code pénal Art. 230
- Netherlands: Wetboek van Strafrecht Artikel 435
- Norway: Lov om straff (straffeloven) § 165 (only the heading could be taken from the fetched page)
- Portugal: Código Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 48/95) Artigo 307 (only the heading could be taken from the fetched page)

The texts of the provisions are quoted in the [survey of the world's laws](../docs/world-law-2026-11-12.md) (in Japanese), "2026-11-12 の続き：当てはめ".
Keeping these rules reduces the possibility that these provisions apply; it does not remove it.

## How to apply

Vercel, which serves the site, and GitHub, which keeps the applications, may use what is placed on them to train AI models. If you are worried about your personal data, do not apply. These uses are described in [Privacy](./privacy.en.md).

1. From 00:00 on 2026-11-22 (Japan time), open an issue with the form [Application for knighthood](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/nusquama/issues/new?template=knighting.yml) (before then, applications are not received under "Pause in receiving applications").
2. Give a public link to the correction, and say what was wrong and how you corrected it.
3. Tick every one of the pledges.

What an applicant agrees to is the version of the rules on the day of the application. That version can be checked in the history of the public repository.

Do not write your real name, address, affiliation or contact details.

## What the operator checks

- That the link is public and reads as a correction.
- That it reads as a correction of the applicant's own mistake.
- That it contains no personal data of others and nothing that hurts others.
- That every pledge in the form is ticked.
- That the linked correction does not state clearly that the applicant lives outside Japan, is outside Japan at the time of applying, holds Italian nationality or the nationality of a country under "Countries that restrict foreign titles", or is under 16. If it does, the operator asks the applicant, and does not knight them unless it is confirmed that they meet the conditions.

The operator does not judge whether the correction itself is right. The operator judges only that a correction was made.

When an application issue is opened or edited, an automatic check looks at the ticks in the form and whether the link to the correction is an https URL that does not point to a refused destination, and comments the result in the issue.
The automatic check does not open the link to the correction. The operator is the one who opens and reads it.
The refused destinations are localhost; names ending in .localhost, .local, .internal, .home.arpa, .test, .example, .invalid or .onion; addresses written as numbers; names without a dot; and URLs that contain a user name or password. None of them points to a public page.
The automatic check decides nothing. The operator decides on knighting.

## What is not checked

The operator does not check nationality, country of residence, age or real name, and asks for no identity document.
Nusquama gives no nationality. Knights are not its people.
Age, country of residence, the country where the applicant is when applying, and not holding Italian nationality or the nationality of a country under "Countries that restrict foreign titles" are taken from the applicant's own declaration, by the ticks in the form.
But what the linked correction clearly states is not overlooked.
The person dealt with is the GitHub account that applied.
If it turns out that an applicant did not meet the conditions, their name is taken off the roll.
If the application was from a person under 16, its issue is also deleted, without being asked.

## What is declined

No knighthood is given for:

- Anything that is not a correction of a mistake (advertising, self-introduction, pointing out someone else's mistake, and so on).
- Anything that cannot be checked (something not public, or a link that does not open).
- Anything that falls under "What is not allowed" in the Terms of Use.
- An application where the linked correction clearly shows that the applicant does not meet the conditions (age, country of residence, the country where the applicant is when applying, or nationality).
- An application opened from 2026-11-12 until 00:00 on 2026-11-22 (Japan time) ("Pause in receiving applications").
- From 2026-11-22, an application where what the applicant wrote, or the linked correction, clearly shows that "The premise of good sense" does not hold.

When declining, the operator writes only one fixed sentence in the issue ("This does not meet the conditions for knighting."), and comments on no one. The issue is deleted if the applicant asks.

## The roll

Those knighted are entered on the [roll of knights](../KNIGHTS.en.md) in the order of their knighting.
On knighting, the operator posts a comment on the application issue with a link to the row of the roll, and closes the issue as completed.
There is only one rank, "knight", with nothing above or below it (Basic Law, Article 7).
The roll gives each knight by account name only. A knight is called "Knight" followed by the account name, with no other title or adornment added.

## Withdrawal and revocation

A knight may ask at any time to be taken off the roll. No reason is needed. On withdrawal, their name is taken off the roll.
The operator may revoke a knighthood when a knight uses the title outside this kingdom ([Terms of Use](./terms.en.md), "Titles"; Basic Law, Article 8) or breaks the Terms of Use. On revocation, the name is taken off the roll.
The kingdom keeps its mistakes, but a person's name is different. A name taken off the roll is not kept even in a record of the revocation, unless the person asks for that.

---

Source: https://nusquama.vercel.app/policies/requests.en.html

# Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal

Last updated: 2026-11-13.

This is an English translation. The [Japanese version](./requests.md) governs; if the two differ, the Japanese version applies.

## What may be asked for

- Withdrawal from the roll of knights (taking the name off).
- Correction or deletion of an entry about oneself on the roll or in an issue.
- Notice of the purpose of use, disclosure, correction, addition, deletion, suspension of use, erasure, or stopping the provision to third parties, of retained personal data about oneself.
- Deletion of one's personal data written without one's consent.
- Deletion of content that harms one's honour or reputation.
- Deletion of content that infringes one's rights (copyright, trademark, likeness and so on).
- A change of wording where Nusquama may be mistaken for something real.

There is no charge.
Requests are received in the same way, and answered as quickly, from people in any country, whatever country they live in and whatever their nationality. They are received in Japanese or in English.

## How to ask

Open an issue with the form [Requests for removal, correction or withdrawal](https://github.com/cpsbvbng26-dotcom/nusquama/issues/new?template=request.yml), and say which entry it concerns and what is asked.
Issues cannot be opened without a form.
The only channel is GitHub. Nusquama has no contact outside GitHub. A free GitHub account is enough.
A request may be made by an agent. In that case, the person concerned writes a word in the issue, from their own GitHub account, that they asked the agent.
Do not copy the personal data in question into the issue. Say only where it is.

## Requests that cannot be made in public

Nusquama has no channel that receives requests privately.
GitHub's private vulnerability reporting is not enabled for this repository (checked through the GitHub API on 2026-11-13).
If there is a reason a request cannot be written in public, choose 「非公開の連絡を求める」 ("Ask for a private contact") as the kind in the form, and leave the rest empty. The issue then shows only the GitHub account name, the title and the kind.
The operator answers privately only when the person who asks has made a contact public on their own GitHub profile, and then answers at that contact.
When there is no such contact, there is no private route. The operator then answers in the issue, without personal details.
A security problem with the site or the repository is reported in the same way ([How to report a security problem](../SECURITY.md)).

## After a request

The operator aims to answer each request within 7 days.
Where the harm is serious, such as exposed personal data, the entry is taken down at once, before any decision.
An entry that harms another person's honour or reputation is also taken down at once, before any decision. After it is taken down, whether that was right is checked.
Withdrawal from the roll is granted whatever the reason.
Requests for disclosure, correction, suspension of use and the like are met without delay. Disclosure is made in the way asked; when an electronic record is asked for, an electronic record is given.
When a request is met, what was done is made known without delay. When the data asked for does not exist, or cannot be given in the way asked, that too is made known without delay.
When a request is not met, the reason is given.

## What cannot be removed

Earlier versions in the repository remain unless its history is rewritten. Copies already made by others are beyond the operator's reach.
Earlier deployments kept at Vercel that contain the entry are deleted from Vercel on request.
Where it must be erased from the history of the repository, the operator asks GitHub to remove it.
